chunks.text: For an object moving with uniform velocity along a straight line, the position-time (x-t) graph is a straight line. The slope of the x-t graph at any instant gives the instantaneous velocity, $v = dx/dt$.

items.subject: physics
items.topic: Kinematic equations for uniformly accelerated motion

chunks.text: For motion with constant acceleration $a$, initial velocity $u$ and final velocity $v$ after displacement $s$: $v = u + at$, $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ and $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$.

source.section: 2.4 Kinematic equations for uniformly accelerated motion

chunks.text: The equation $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ is useful when time is not given. A body starting from rest has $u = 0$.
